name: Private credit stress
value: Nontraded BDC exit requests above 5% caps
summary: Redemption requests at nontraded BDCs stay above their usual 5% quarterly caps; no wave of gates or forced sales found
state: Fitch found that 13 of 15 perpetual nontraded BDCs received third-quarter redemption requests averaging 9.8% of shares, above their usual 5% quarterly caps (InvestmentNews). Client redemptions from nontraded BDCs reached $12.7bn in the first half of 2026, and managers hope to bring them below 5% of NAV by mid-2027 (InvestmentNews, 18 Nov). Searches on 25 Nov found no simultaneous gating by several large funds, forced asset sales or losses spreading to banks or insurers, so Watch holds.
for_you: Holders of semi-liquid private credit funds may find withdrawals limited to a fixed share each quarter. Wider banking and insurance markets show no sign of contagion so far.
rubric_hit: Watch: large funds limiting redemptions (requests ~9.8% vs 5% caps); no multi-fund gating or bank losses for Alert

sources.title: InvestmentNews — After a tough year, are private credit funds and BDCs in line for a comeback in 2027?
InvestmentNews — Pace of investors selling nontraded BDCs slows but remains significant, says Fitch

why: Private credit has grown fast outside bank regulation; its losses surface late and can spill into banks, insurers and pension funds.
drivers: Defaults among leveraged mid-sized borrowers, payment-in-kind interest, fund redemption requests, bank lending to funds.

rubric.alert: Several large funds gate at once, forced asset sales, or losses spreading to banks or insurers.
rubric.watch: A large fund limits redemptions, listed BDCs trade at wide discounts to NAV, or a cluster of borrower defaults with heavy losses.
rubric.normal: No notable fund gates, defaults or markdowns beyond the routine.
